mainTopic: The כהן גדול's טבילות and קידושין on יום הכפורים, and the meaning of קרצו in the שחיטה of the תמיד
overview: The גמרא looks for the source that the כהן גדול must immerse (טבילה) each time he switches between בגדי זהב and בגדי לבן on יום הכפורים. Two קל וחומר arguments fail, because each set of garments has its own advantage. So the sources are פסוקים: 'כתנת בד קדש ילבש' for the switch into white, and 'בגדי קדש הם ורחץ... ולבשם' for the switch back to gold. A ברייתא lists the five services and their garments. It then learns from 'ופשט... ורחץ, ורחץ... ולבש' that each טבילה needs two קידושין of hands and feet, and that the טבילה must be done במקום קדוש. רבי יהודה learns קידוש from the קל וחומר of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון instead. רב חסדא and רב אחא בר יעקב disagree about whether the קידוש is done while dressed or undressed, and the two readings cannot be combined, or there would be fifteen קידושין. Finally, the גמרא explains that the משנה's word קרצו means slaughtering, and that the כהן גדול cut most of both סימנים. It uses ריש לקיש's statement to show this, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A logical argument that white garments need immersion
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל uses a קל וחומר: if the less-holy בגדי זהב need טבילה, then the בגדי לבן, which are worn into the קודש הקדשים, surely need it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught a קל וחומר: The golden garments are not worn into the Holy of Holies, yet they require immersion. So the white garments, which ARE worn into the Holy of Holies, surely require immersion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to prove from logic that the כהן גדול must immerse before putting on the בגדי לבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that בגדי זהב need טבילה. The argument says the בגדי לבן are holier because they are worn into the קודש הקדשים. If the weaker case needs טבילה, the stronger case should need it even more.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger case
The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
The golden garments the כהן גדול wears all year
The white linen garments worn for the special יום הכפורים service
The innermost place, the קודש הקדשים

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, קַל וָחוֹמֶר:
phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: an a fortiori argument:
Just as the golden garments,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין כֹּהֵן נִכְנָס בָּהֶן לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים —
phrases.english: in which the priest does not enter the innermost sanctum,
require immersion,

phrases.aramaic: בִּגְדֵי לָבָן שֶׁנִּכְנָס בָּהֶן לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים —
phrases.english: then the white garments, in which he does enter the innermost sanctum,
is it not logical that they require immersion!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.raayaObject: That changing from בגדי זהב to בגדי לבן requires טבילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר based on the greater holiness of entering the קודש הקדשים

steps.title: The golden garments have a different advantage
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is refuted: בגדי זהב have their own strength, because they bring atonement all year long.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: The golden garments are special because the atonement they bring is greater!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the קל וחומר from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'weaker' case is weaker in every way. But בגדי זהב are used for כפרה all year, while בגדי לבן are used only on one day. So maybe that is why בגדי זהב need טבילה, and the logic does not carry over to בגדי לבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Their atonement is greater, used much more often

steps.confusionAlert: Each set of garments is 'stronger' in a different way. בגדי לבן enter the קודש הקדשים, while בגדי זהב bring more frequent כפרה. That is why neither one can serve as the clear 'weaker' case.

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
What about golden garments?
They are special because their atonement is extensive!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire קל וחומר for בגדי לבן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בגדי זהב have a strength of their own (greater כפרה), so they are not clearly the weaker case

steps.title: The source is רבי's verse instead
steps.stepSummary: Since the logic failed, the גמרא concludes that the source comes from רבי's derivation from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he derives it from the teaching of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the logical argument and says the rule comes from רבי's verse, which it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once logic cannot prove the rule, the גמרא turns to a direct source in the תורה. This also sets up the next step, where רבי's teaching is analyzed.

phrases.english: Rather, he derives it from the teaching of Rabbi.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: טבילה when changing into בגדי לבן comes from רבי's פסוק, not from a קל וחומר

steps.title: רבי's source for five immersions and ten washings
steps.stepSummary: רבי derives the five טבילות and ten קידושין of יום הכפורים from 'כתנת בד קדש ילבש', which teaches that anyone switching between services needs טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: Where do we learn the five immersions and ten hand-and-foot washings that the כהן גדול does on יום הכפורים? The פסוק says: 'He shall wear a holy linen tunic.' From this you learn that anyone who switches from one service to another needs immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי's teaching, the source it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול switches garments five times on יום הכפורים, and each switch needs one טבילה. Each switch also needs two washings of hands and feet, one before and one after, which makes ten. The פסוק links putting on the linen tunic with washing, which teaches that a switch into בגדי לבן requires טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The five immersions of the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים
Ten washings of hands and feet from the כיור
One who switches from one service to another

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule behind the whole סדר העבודה of יום הכפורים: every change of garments requires a טבילה.

phrases.english: Rabbi said: From where do we know the five immersions
and ten sanctifications (of hands and feet)

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁטּוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: that the High Priest immerses and sanctifies on that day?
The verse teaches:
"He shall wear a holy linen tunic",
from this you have learned
that anyone who changes from one service to another
requires immersion.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Switching from one service to another requires טבילה, derived from 'כתנת בד קדש ילבש'

steps.title: What about switching back to golden garments?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי's פסוק covers switching from gold to white, and asks for the source for switching from white back to gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for going from golden garments to white garments. From where do we know that going from white garments to golden garments needs immersion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the opposite direction, which sets up the next attempt at a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's פסוק talks about putting on the linen garments, so it only proves the switch into בגדי לבן. The return to בגדי זהב still needs its own source.

phrases.english: We found from golden garments to white garments;
from white garments to golden garments, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן מִבִּגְדֵי זָהָב לְבִגְדֵי לָבָן, מִבִּגְדֵי לָבָן לְבִגְדֵי זָהָב מִנַּיִן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for טבילה when switching from בגדי לבן to בגדי זהב

steps.title: A reverse logical argument for golden garments
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל offers a קל וחומר: if בגדי לבן, with less כפרה, need טבילה, then בגדי זהב, with more כפרה, surely do.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught a קל וחומר: The white garments bring less atonement, yet they require immersion. So the golden garments, which bring more atonement, surely require immersion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with logic, using the reverse of the first קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the strength being used is the greater כפרה of בגדי זהב. Since בגדי לבן already need טבילה, the argument says בגדי זהב should need it even more.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, קַל וָחוֹמֶר:
phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: an a fortiori argument:
Just as the white garments,
whose atonement is not extensive,
require immersion,
then the golden garments, whose atonement is extensive,
is it not logical that they require immersion?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the greater כפרה of בגדי זהב

steps.title: White garments have their own advantage
steps.stepSummary: This קל וחומר is also refuted, because בגדי לבן are worn into the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: The white garments are special because he enters the Holy of Holies in them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בגדי לבן have a holiness of their own, since they enter the קודש הקדשים. That may be why they need טבילה, so we cannot conclude anything about בגדי זהב.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because they have a special feature

steps.whatToRemember: Both קל וחומר arguments fail for the same reason: each set of garments has its own unique advantage.

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
What about white garments?
They are special because he enters the innermost sanctum in them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the second קל וחומר
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר for בגדי זהב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בגדי לבן have a unique strength (entering the קודש הקדשים)

steps.title: The verse teaches immersion for all holy garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the source is the ברייתא's next פסוק, 'בגדי קדש הם ורחץ... ולבשם', which requires טבילה before putting on any holy garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא teaches when it says 'and it also says': 'They are holy garments, and he shall wash his flesh in water and put them on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer: the switch back to בגדי זהב is learned from the פסוק quoted later in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בגדי קדש הם' are general and cover all holy garments, not only the linen ones. So any change into holy garments, including back into בגדי זהב, needs טבילה. This explains why the ברייתא added a second פסוק with 'ואומר'.

keyTerms.meaning: And the verse also says (introducing an additional source)

steps.whatToRemember: Changing into בגדי לבן needs טבילה because of 'כתנת בד קדש ילבש'. Changing back to בגדי זהב needs טבילה because of 'בגדי קדש הם ורחץ... ולבשם'. Logic (קל וחומר) could not prove either direction.

phrases.english: This is what is taught:
"And it says:
'They are holy garments,
and he shall wash his flesh in water and put them on.'"

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Switching from בגדי לבן to בגדי זהב requires טבילה, learned from 'בגדי קדש הם ורחץ... ולבשם'

steps.title: The five services of יום הכפורים and their garments
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the five עבודות of the day in order, alternating between בגדי זהב and בגדי לבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are five services: the morning תמיד in gold garments, the special service of the day in white garments, his ram and the people's ram in gold garments, the spoon and coal pan in white garments, and the afternoon תמיד in gold garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out the five services that the כהן גדול does on יום הכפורים, and which set of clothes he wears for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garments switch back and forth: זהב, לבן, זהב, לבן, זהב. Every switch is a new service, and each one needs a טבילה. That is why there are five טבילות.

keyTerms.meaning: The special יום הכפורים service (פר and שעיר)
His own ram and the ram of the people (עולות)
The spoon of קטורת and the coal pan, taken out of the קודש הקדשים
The gold garments / the white linen garments of the כהן גדול

steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the map behind the five טבילות and ten קידושין. Each service is one טבילה, and each טבילה comes with two קידושין.

phrases.english: And they are five services:
The morning daily offering, in gold garments;
the service of the day, in white garments;
his ram and the people's ram, in gold garments;
the spoon and coal pan, in white garments;

phrases.aramaic: תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם בְּבִגְדֵי זָהָב.
phrases.english: the afternoon daily offering, in gold garments.
phrases.notes: These five services alternate gold, white, gold, white, gold. Each change of garments needs its own טבילה, which gives five טבילות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 4 by listing the five services behind the five טבילות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five עבודות of יום הכפורים alternate between gold and white garments.

steps.title: Source that each immersion needs two hand-and-foot washings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that every טבילה needs two קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that each and every immersion needs two washings of the hands and feet?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks where we learn that each טבילה goes with two קידושין. This sets up the next move, where a פסוק is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five טבילות times two קידושין gives the ten קידושין. The question is about the 'two': one קידוש when taking off the old clothes and one when putting on the new ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Washing the hands and feet from the כיור
Immersing the whole body in a מקוה

phrases.english: And from where do we know that each and every immersion
requires two sanctifications (of hands and feet)?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁכׇּל טְבִילָה וּטְבִילָה צְרִיכָה שְׁנֵי קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the five טבילות to the source of the ten קידושין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for two קידושין with each טבילה.

steps.title: Washing after removing and before putting on
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns the two קידושין from the 'ורחץ' that sits between 'ופשט' and 'ולבש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he shall remove... and he shall wash,' and 'And he shall wash... and put on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the פסוקים about the כהן גדול changing clothes. One washing is tied to taking off, and another is tied to putting on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read 'ופשט... ורחץ' as a washing when he takes off his clothes. Read 'ורחץ... ולבש' as a washing before he puts on his clothes. That gives two קידושין for each change.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'And he shall remove... and he shall wash,'
phrases.notes: A washing linked to taking off the clothes.

phrases.english: 'And he shall wash... and put on.'
phrases.notes: A washing linked to putting on the clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא ט״ז:כ״ג-כ״ד: a washing tied to removing and a washing tied to dressing.

steps.title: But that verse speaks about immersion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the washing in this פסוק means טבילה, not קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is written about immersion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. 'ורחץ את בשרו' means washing the whole body, which is טבילה, not washing the hands and feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is about טבילה, it cannot be the source for קידוש ידים ורגלים. So the source in step 11 seems to prove the wrong thing.

phrases.english: That is written about immersion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ורחץ את בשרו' means a full-body טבילה, so it cannot teach hand-and-foot קידוש.

steps.title: Since immersion is already known, apply it to washing
steps.stepSummary: Since טבילה is already learned from 'בגדי קדש הם', this פסוק is free to teach קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is not needed for immersion, which we learn from 'they are holy garments,' apply it to sanctification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the rule 'אם אינו ענין'. We already have a source for טבילה, so this extra פסוק is moved over to teach קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that 'בגדי קדש הם' already requires טבילה for every change of clothes. A פסוק is never written for nothing, so this 'ורחץ' must teach something else, which is קידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this matter (so it is moved to another matter)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the פסוק never speaks of טבילה in its plain words. It says the טבילה law is already covered elsewhere, so the teaching of this פסוק is moved over to קידוש.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of immersion,
which is derived from 'they are holy garments,'
apply it to the matter of sanctification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting an extra פסוק (אם אינו ענין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only teaches טבילה, so it cannot teach קידוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: טבילה is already known from 'בגדי קדש הם', so this פסוק teaches the two קידושין.

steps.title: Why not write it as hand-and-foot washing?
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק teaches קידוש, why does the Torah use the language of טבילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the Merciful One write it in the language of sanctification!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. If the פסוק really means קידוש, the Torah should have written it as hand-and-foot washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using body-washing words to teach hand-washing looks strange. The גמרא wants a reason for this wording.

phrases.english: Then let the Merciful One write it in the language of sanctification!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13 based on the wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the meaning is קידוש, using טבילה words seems unexplained.

steps.title: Immersion must be in a holy place, like washing
steps.stepSummary: The טבילה wording teaches that טבילה is like קידוש: both must be done במקום קדוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that immersion is like sanctification. Just as sanctification is done in a holy place, so too immersion is done in a holy place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the wording. The פסוק links טבילה to קידוש to teach a new law about where the טבילה is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידוש is done at the כיור, which stands in the עזרה. Because the Torah wrote the קידוש law with טבילה words, טבילה gets the same rule. The כהן גדול's טבילות must be done inside the holy area, not outside the מקדש.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'ורחץ' פסוקים teach two things: two קידושין for every טבילה, and that the טבילה must be done במקום קדוש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the כהן גדול's טבילות on יום הכפורים take place in the בית הטבילה on the roof of בית הפרוה, inside the holy area.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that immersion is like sanctification:
just as sanctification is in a holy place,
so too immersion is in a holy place.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דִּטְבִילָה כְּקִידּוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording teaches an extra law
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording teaches that טבילה, like קידוש, must be done במקום קדוש.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn the washing?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה uses this פסוק for טבילה, where does he learn קידוש?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, from where does he learn sanctification?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about רבי יהודה, who uses this 'ורחץ' פסוק as his source for טבילה. Then it is not free to teach קידוש, so he needs another source. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'אם אינו ענין' answer only works for someone who learns טבילה from 'בגדי קדש הם'. For רבי יהודה the פסוק is still needed for טבילה, so the question of where קידוש comes from opens again.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who learns טבילה from this verse itself
From where does he derive it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda,
from where does he derive sanctification?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 13's answer does not fit רבי יהודה's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה's source for the קידושין.

steps.title: From רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns קידוש from the קל וחומר of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He derives it from the teaching of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה gets קידוש from a different source: the reasoning of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reasons with a קל וחומר. Where the Torah does not require טבילה, it still requires קידוש. So where it does require טבילה for every change of clothes, it surely requires קידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose קל וחומר teaches קידוש

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees there are two קידושין with each טבילה. They only disagree about the source: the 'ורחץ' פסוק, or for רבי יהודה, the קל וחומר of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: He derives it from Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: This refers to his קל וחומר: if קידוש is required where there is no טבילה, then surely where there is טבילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns קידוש from the קל וחומר of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי's view differs from both רבי מאיר and the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that רבי holds the כהן does קידוש while undressed. This is unlike the רבנן and unlike רבי מאיר, who both have him do it while dressed, at least for the last קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: רבי's opinion is different from רבי מאיר and from the רבנן. It is different from the רבנן because they say he washes while dressed, and רבי says he washes while undressing. It is different from רבי מאיר because רבי מאיר says the last washing is done while dressed, and רבי says it is done while undressing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא compares רבי's opinion to the two other opinions and shows that it stands on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the כהן washes his hands and feet while wearing the clothes or while undressed. The רבנן say both washings happen while dressed. רבי מאיר says at least the last one happens while dressed. According to רב חסדא, רבי has both washings done while undressed, so he disagrees with both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: The last washing of hands and feet

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This view of Rabbi differs from Rabbi Meir,
and differs from the Rabbis.
It differs from the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ רַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: כְּשֶׁהוּא לָבוּשׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: because the Rabbis say: he washes while dressed,
and he (Rabbi) says: he washes while undressing.
And it differs from Rabbi Meir:
because Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: הָךְ קִידּוּשׁ בָּתְרָא כְּשֶׁהוּא לָבוּשׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: this last washing, he does while dressed,
and he (Rabbi) says: he washes while undressing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 16-17 dealt with רבי יהודה's source. רב חסדא now returns to רבי's ברייתא (steps 4 and 11, 'ופשט... ורחץ', 'ורחץ... ולבש') and shows what it implies about when the קידוש is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, both קידושים are done while the כהן is undressed.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the second washing is after dressing
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says that all opinions, including רבי, agree that the second קידוש is done after putting on the clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Everyone agrees about the second washing that he first gets dressed and then washes.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives his own reading. In his view, the second washing is done after dressing according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not what רב חסדא said about רבי. רב חסדא had רבי doing both washings while undressed. רב אחא says that even רבי agrees the second washing comes after dressing.

keyTerms.meaning: The second washing of hands and feet

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Everyone agrees about the second washing
that he dresses and afterwards washes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different picture from רב חסדא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every opinion holds that the second קידוש is done after dressing.

steps.title: The verse shows washing must be right before serving
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'או בגשתם אל המזבח' teaches that the washing is done by a כהן who is missing only the approach to the altar, so he must already be dressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The פסוק says: 'Or when they approach the altar.' This means someone who is missing only the approaching. That leaves out someone who is still missing both dressing and approaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רב אחא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links washing to the moment of approaching the מזבח. So the washing belongs at the point where nothing is left except going to serve. A כהן who still has to get dressed is not yet at that point.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says: 'Or when they approach the altar,'
one who is lacking only the approach,
excluding this one who lacks dressing and approach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אחא's rule with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The second קידוש is done after dressing.

steps.title: רב חסדא and רב אחא cannot both be right
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא says that the two readings cannot be combined. If they were, רבי would require fifteen קידושים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: רב חסדא does not hold like רב אחא, and רב אחא does not hold like רב חסדא. If they did, then according to רבי there would be fifteen washings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the two opinions really disagree and cannot be joined together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combining them would give three washings for each change of clothes. There would be two while undressed, following רב חסדא, plus one after dressing, following רב אחא. With five changes of clothes on יום כיפור, that comes to fifteen, which contradicts רבי's own count of ten קידושין (step 4). So each אמורא rejects the other's reading of רבי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that רב אחא is arguing with רבי himself. The disagreement is only about how to read רבי, and the two readings exclude each other.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַב חִסְדָּא אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda does not hold like Rav Acha,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַב אַחָא אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא.
phrases.english: and Rav Acha does not hold like Rav Chisda.
For if so,
according to Rabbi there would be fifteen washings.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַב חִסְדָּא אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the relationship between the two readings.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא and רב אחא are two separate, competing readings of רבי. Combining them would wrongly produce fifteen קידושים.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, רבי has both washings while undressed. According to רב אחא, the second washing is after dressing. The two views cannot be combined.

steps.title: What does the word קרצו mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the תמיד being brought to the כהן גדול and asks what 'קרצו' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: They brought him the תמיד, and he did 'קרצו', and so on. What does 'קרצו' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks about an unusual word in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. The question is about the meaning of a single word, קרצו, which describes what the כהן גדול did to the תמיד.

phrases.aramaic: הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַתָּמִיד קְרָצוֹ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: They brought him the daily offering, he 'keratz-ed' it, etc.
What is 'keratzo'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה for a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word קרצו.

steps.title: קרצו means killing
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that קרצו is a word that means killing, so here it refers to slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is a word that means killing.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question about the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרצו means the כהן גדול slaughtered the תמיד himself. The proof that the word means this comes in the next steps.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
It is a term of killing.

steps.title: A verse in ירמיה uses the word קרץ
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a פסוק in ירמיה where the word 'קרץ' appears, as a source for עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What is the source? 'Egypt is a very beautiful calf, but קרץ from the north is coming, coming.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support עולא's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קרץ in this פסוק describes what comes against מצרים from the north. If it means killers, that supports עולא. The next step asks how we know it means that.

keyTerms.meaning: The word in the verse being used as a proof

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, מַאי קְרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: What is the verse?
'Egypt is a very beautiful calf,
keretz from the north is coming, coming.'

steps.title: How does the verse show it means killing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that קרץ in this פסוק means killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What shows that this is the meaning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the proof works, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just quoting the פסוק does not prove the meaning, because קרץ could mean something else there. The גמרא wants evidence for how to read the word.

keyTerms.meaning: What indicates this? / How is it implied?

phrases.english: What indicates it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: How we know קרץ in the פסוק means killing.

steps.title: רב יוסף's translation proves the meaning
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's תרגום renders קרץ as 'murderous nations', which shows the word means killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף translates it: 'Egypt was a beautiful kingdom; murderous nations from the north will come upon it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting the Aramaic translation of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרגום translates קרץ as 'עממין קטולין', which means killing nations. This confirms that קרץ is a word of killing, so עולא's explanation of קרצו stands.

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef translates:
'Egypt was a beautiful kingdom,
murderous nations
from the north will come upon it.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרגום renders קרץ as killing nations, which proves the meaning.

steps.title: How much did he cut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much of the slaughter the כהן גדול himself did.
steps.simpleTranslation: He slaughtered it, to what extent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about how far the כהן גדול's slaughtering went.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the כהן גדול did קרצו, and then someone else finished the slaughter. The question is how much cutting he did before handing it over.

phrases.english: He slaughtered it, to what extent?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much of the cut the כהן גדול made.

steps.title: He cut most of both signs
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the כהן גדול cut most of both סימנים, the windpipe and the food pipe, which is enough for a valid שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Through most of the two signs.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers that the כהן גדול himself made a complete, valid slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting most of the windpipe and most of the food pipe is what makes a שחיטה kosher. So the כהן גדול did the full שחיטה himself. The other כהן only finished the cut afterwards.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the two signs (windpipe and food pipe)
The windpipe and food pipe cut in שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: קרצו means slaughtering, as shown from ירמיה and רב יוסף's תרגום. The כהן גדול cut most of both סימנים, which is a complete שחיטה.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
With most of the two (signs).

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He cut most of both סימנים, a complete valid שחיטה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees: most of both organs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also rules that the כהן גדול's cut was רוב שנים, most of both סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, רבי יוחנן said: the כהן גדול cut most of both organs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second אמורא, רבי יוחנן, who agrees with עולא that the כהן גדול cut most of both סימנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 gave עולא's answer: the כהן גדול cut most of the windpipe and the food pipe. Now רבי יוחנן is quoted as saying the same thing, so עולא's view gains support. No new detail is added. The step only strengthens what was already said.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly said (introduces someone who agrees)
Most of both organs (the windpipe and the food pipe)
The two organs that must be cut in שחיטה: the windpipe and the food pipe

phrases.english: And similarly, Rabbi Yochanan said:
With the majority of the two organs.
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול cut most of each of the two סימנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second אמורא agrees with עולא's answer in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול cut רוב שנים, most of both סימנים.

steps.title: ריש לקיש also holds most of both, shown by his question about the extra wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says ריש לקיש agrees and brings his statement as proof. He asks why the laws of שחיטה needed to say 'most of one in a bird, most of two in an animal' when 'most of one is like all of it' was already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש also held: most of both organs. As ריש לקיש said: Since we already learned that most of one organ counts like the whole organ, why did we also need to learn 'most of one in a bird and most of two in an animal'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says ריש לקיש also holds רוב שנים and starts quoting his statement as proof. The quote opens with a question that sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that most of a סימן counts like the whole סימן. We also know that a bird needs one סימן cut and an animal needs two. Putting those together already tells us 'most of one for a bird, most of two for an animal.' So ריש לקיש asks why it had to be said again. His answer will show that he holds most of both is enough for our case.

keyTerms.meaning: And also (adds another person who agrees)
Most of one is like all of it
Why did we learn it? (asks why a teaching is needed)

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not doubting the law. He agrees that a bird needs most of one and an animal needs most of two. He is only asking why it had to be stated, since it already follows from rules we know.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish also held:
With the majority of the two organs,
as Reish Lakish said:
Since we already learned:
the majority of one organ is like the whole of it,
why did we learn:
the majority of one organ in a bird
and the majority of two organs in an animal?
phrases.notes: This seems to follow already from known rules, so why say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ סָבַר בְּרוֹב שְׁנַיִם, דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third authority joins עולא and רבי יוחנן, this time proven from his own statement.
steps.raayaObject: That ריש לקיש holds the כהן גדול cut רוב שנים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's statement explaining why the wording 'most of two in an animal' was needed.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's answer: the extra wording is needed for the תמיד case
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the extra wording is needed because of our משנה. There, the כהן גדול cut most of the way and another כהן finished. Without the wording, we might have thought the slaughter was פסול if the other כהן did not finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we learned: They brought him the תמיד. He cut most of the way, another כהן finished the slaughter for him, and he received the blood and sprinkled it. Without this teaching, I might have thought that if the other כהן did not finish, the offering would be פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers his own question. The wording 'most of two in an animal' is needed so that no one thinks the תמיד of יום הכפורים is פסול when the other כהן did not finish cutting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says another כהן finished the cut. That could make someone think finishing is required, so leaving it unfinished would be פסול. The extra wording teaches that most of both סימנים is already a complete שחיטה. This shows that ריש לקיש holds the כהן גדול cut רוב שנים.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offering brought every morning and afternoon
He slaughtered it, cutting most of both סימנים (as explained in steps 23-28)
And he sprinkled it (the blood on the מזבח)
I might have thought (introduces a wrong idea the teaching rules out)

phrases.english: Because we learned:
They brought him the daily offering,
he cut it,
phrases.notes: He cut most of both organs.

phrases.english: and another כהן completed the slaughter for him,
and he received the blood and sprinkled it.
I might have thought: if the other did not complete it,
it would be invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ: הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַתָּמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question ריש לקיש asked in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the extra wording 'most of two in an animal' was needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To rule out the idea that the תמיד is פסול if the other כהן did not finish the cut.

steps.title: How could finishing ever be required if another priest may not serve?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's idea that finishing might have been needed. If finishing were a real part of the service, then another כהן would be doing a יום הכפורים service, and those services are valid only through the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I might have thought that if he did not finish, it would be פסול'? If so, the finishing would be a service done by someone else. And we learned: all the services of יום הכפורים are valid only when done by the כהן גדול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats ריש לקיש's words 'I might have thought it would be פסול' and attacks them. Finishing cannot be a required part of the service, because another כהן did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If leaving the cut unfinished made the offering פסול, then the finishing would be part of the real service. But another כהן finished it, and all יום הכפורים services must be done by the כהן גדול. So it makes no sense to suggest that finishing is required. That means ריש לקיש's 'I might have thought' seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem that follows from the idea)
A service done by someone else, not the כהן גדול
And we learned (quoting a teaching of the תנאים)
The special services of יום הכפורים

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא repeats ריש לקיש's words on purpose. This time they are being challenged, not explained.

phrases.english: 'I might have thought: if he did not complete it, it would be invalid'?!
If so, it would be
a service done by another,
and we learned: all the services of Yom Kippur
are valid only when done by him (the כהן גדול)!

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא מֵירַק יְהֵא פָּסוּל?! אִם כֵּן הָוְיָא לֵיהּ עֲבוֹדָה בְּאַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'I might have thought' that ריש לקיש used in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's suggestion that the offering might have been פסול if the other כהן did not finish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If finishing were required, it would be a service done by another כהן, but all יום הכפורים services must be done by the כהן גדול. So finishing cannot be required, even as a mistaken possibility.

steps.title: ריש לקיש meant it might be invalid only rabbinically
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that ריש לקיש meant the offering might have been thought פסול only מדרבנן, not by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: I might have thought it would be פסול by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing ריש לקיש's words. The mistaken idea was only that the offering would be פסול מדרבנן. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, finishing is clearly not needed, so there is no problem of another כהן doing a real service. The only possible mistake was to think the חכמים made it פסול when the cut was left unfinished. The extra wording 'most of two in an animal' rules out even that.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (the גמרא re-reads a statement)
By rabbinic law, not by Torah law
Invalid (an offering that does not count)

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
I might have thought it would be invalid by rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: יָכוֹל יְהֵא פָּסוּל מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 32 by re-reading ריש לקיש's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the statement: the 'פסול' meant only rabbinic, not Torah law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש meant the offering might be פסול by Torah law, which would make the finishing a real service done by another כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant only that it might be פסול מדרבנן. By Torah law, most of both סימנים is a complete שחיטה, so the other כהן is not doing a required service.
